Evidence Summary: Now Assist AI agents autonomously triage incoming service requests, execute multi-step diagnostic investigations, and remediate incidents end-to-end without manual intervention. Self-executing agentic workflows can be triggered automatically (via schedule, system events, or user intent) to analyze context, use configured tools, and execute actions across workflows and enterprise records.
Evaluation Notes: Operates autonomously across ITSM, CSM, and HRSD workflows without requiring manual invocation.

Evidence Summary: ServiceNow's AI Agent Orchestrator plans and coordinates tasks across AI agents, while individual agents use domain-tuned Now LLM reasoning engines, prompt-chaining, record context, searchable CMDB data, knowledge articles, and LLM-generated next-best actions to analyze unstructured incident logs, set intermediate goals, and execute remediation subflows.
Evaluation Notes: Supports dynamic reasoning and execution across structured CMDB data, business logic, and unstructured knowledge content.

Evidence Summary: Agentic workflows coordinate multi-step, cross-departmental actions using Flow Designer, Process Automation Designer, Playbooks, and the AI Agent Orchestrator. Workflows leverage triggers, tools, modular action blocks, and prebuilt agentic flow templates that can execute on a schedule, on demand, or in response to system events.
Evaluation Notes: Provides visual drag-and-drop orchestration templates alongside automatic trigger activation and AI-driven control flow.

Evidence Summary: ServiceNow provides long-term semantic memory that retains user-specific facts across interactions, while AI Agent Orchestrator and Now Assist maintain short-term session memory during execution. Context is assembled by combining dialogue history with grounding from the ServiceNow Configuration Management Database (CMDB), user profiles, and active records.
Evaluation Notes: Combines short-term workflow tracking with persistent long-term semantic user memory and CMDB grounding.

Evidence Summary: AI agents feature episodic memory learning, converting execution outcomes, past failures, and fixes into experience applied to future tasks. Now Assist Analytics, skill evaluation tools, and user feedback metrics (thumbs up/down) in the Now Assist Admin Console track acceptance rates to iteratively refine skills and prompts.
Evaluation Notes: Combines episodic outcome-based learning loops with administrator-guided prompt/skill evaluation and refinement.

Evidence Summary: AI Agent Orchestrator coordinates multiple specialized domain agents (such as IT Service Desk, Case Triage, and Security Operations agents), managing task sequencing, context sharing, handoffs, and delegation across complex enterprise workflows.
Evaluation Notes: Multi-agent architecture enables collaboration and task delegation across IT, HR, and customer service domains.

Evidence Summary: AI Agent Studio, Now Assist Skill Kit, and Creator Studio provide guided low-code/no-code visual builders to define agent roles, instructions, tools, memory, and access channels. The platform also supports natural-language agent creation in its Prime tier and prompt-based skill authoring.
Evaluation Notes: Enables citizen and pro developers to build and configure custom agents and skills visually or via natural language.

Evidence Summary: The ServiceNow AI Platform and Generative AI Controller support the proprietary Now LLM Service as well as third-party model providers including Microsoft Azure OpenAI, Google Cloud (Gemini), AWS (Claude), OpenAI, and IBM watsonx. Model selection can be assigned per skill or use case.
Evaluation Notes: Out-of-the-box model support varies across specific prebuilt skills and agentic workflows.

Evidence Summary: AI Agent Studio provides guided setup for roles, triggers, channels, and memory, while AI Agent Advisor proposes or generates agents from instance data. Now Assist for Creator adds App Generation, Flow Generation from text prompts, Code Generation in Studio/VS Code, and Automated Testing Framework (ATF) support.
Evaluation Notes: Comprehensive developer tooling combining generative coding, automated flow drafting, and automated testing.

Evidence Summary: Agents integrate with enterprise systems via Integration Hub (hundreds of prebuilt spokes), REST/SOAP APIs, OpenAPI imports, RPA Hub connectors, and record operations. The MCP Client enables agents to connect to external MCP servers, while the MCP Server Console exposes ServiceNow functionality to external AI applications.
Evaluation Notes: Supports bi-directional synchronous/asynchronous API execution and native Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling.

Evidence Summary: Built on a multi-instance architecture with data segregation across global datacenters, the platform supports multi-tenant cloud instances, dedicated private sovereign clouds, FedRAMP High / DoD IL5 environments, and hybrid deployments managed via standard lifecycle and change review processes.
Evaluation Notes: Supports managed enterprise cloud and government/sovereign cloud instances; does not support arbitrary self-hosted runtime deployment.

Evidence Summary: AI agents support supervised execution mode, pausing for user input, answering questions, or requiring human approval before critical tools execute. Workflows also support guided approvals, editable AI draft responses (e.g., ticket updates, emails), and seamless handoffs to live human service agents.
Evaluation Notes: Enforces pre-action human approvals for sensitive actions and seamless handoffs preserving context.

Evidence Summary: ServiceNow provides historical workflow run traces, step-level processing messages, AI Agent Analytics (usage, efficiency, token consumption, error rates), Generative AI Controller execution logs, and AI Control Tower for centralized oversight of agent activity and assets.
Evaluation Notes: Delivers comprehensive operational tracing and telemetry; this is not formal model-feature attribution or causal explainability.

Evidence Summary: Security is enforced through platform ACLs, role-based access control (RBAC), AI-user identities, role masking, and runtime guardrails. Sensitive Data Handler detects and masks PII before sending prompts, and AI Control Tower provides centralized asset governance, compliance oversight, and lifecycle management.
Evaluation Notes: Enterprise-grade governance combining inline PII masking, identity segregation, and compliance auditing.

Evidence Summary: Built on ServiceNow's Advanced High Availability multi-instance architecture and RaptorDB high-throughput data store, the platform scales globally across datacenters to handle millions of workflow transactions, petabyte-scale data, and high-concurrency enterprise sessions.
Evaluation Notes: Proven high-availability enterprise scalability across global multi-instance datacenter infrastructure.

Evidence Summary: Purpose-built agentic workflows and pre-trained models cover IT Service Management (ITSM), Customer Service Management (CSM), HR Service Delivery (HRSD), Field Service Management (FSM), and Security Operations (SecOps) for tasks like incident triage, resolution planning, and task classification.
Evaluation Notes: Deep vertical workflows mapping directly to standard enterprise business processes and departments.

Evidence Summary: A commissioned Forrester TEI study demonstrated up to 400% ROI over three years, accelerated incident resolution, and significant deflection. ServiceNow's internal deployment achieved 410,000 hours saved annually, $17.7M in cost avoidance, and 2.3M employee hours saved in 2025 (with 89% self-service resolution).
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates strong financial and operational ROI; vendor-reported metrics combine AI agents with broader platform AI capabilities.
